newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain lowers rate 25 bps.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain lowers rate 25 bps.

text.p: The Bank of Spain cut 25 basis points off its key money market rate on Thursday, taking it to a historic low of six percent.
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH MADRID

"This measure shows that the Bank of Spain is fairly confident about the future of inflation. One will have to be more aggressive in relation to the Bank of Spain's policies this year. The strength of the peseta in recent days may also have contributed. In any case, it is good news."
BELEN MATEOS, ECONOMIST AT ANALISTAS FINANCIEROS

"In principle, we didn't expect it for today, although it is not a great surprise because there are many factors that explain it. In the first place, the CPI number for December was very good, but in addition, there is the peseta's (strength).

"We think that in a short time, by March, there will be another cut of a half point. The Bank of Spain has focused, principally, on price developments and perhaps it is anticipating favourable expectations for the evolution of prices in coming months."
JUAN ANTONIO MIELGO, ECONOMIST BANK OF AMERICA MADRID

"It's a sign that the Bank of Spain is there and that if inflation, which is key, continues along a good path, the central bank will continue to lower rates. Perhaps the peseta level has also influenced the decision, in order to relieve pressure, although I don't think that it will manage short term because 25 basis points isn't very much. Finally, they mainly have wanted to give some support to a market that at these high levels is somewhat tired as we saw yesterday."
LUCA JELLINEK PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS LONDON
"The move was a little bit surprising for the market. You can see that from the weighted average rate, which is pretty high at 6.22 percent compared with the marginal one (of 6.00 pct).

"After yesterday's CPI people thought that the central bank would have waited more before cutting the rate. But the peseta is so strong.... And it will remain strong because nobody is going to think this will be the last cut of the year. It is just the first one."
ALVARO XIMENEN DE EMBUN, BOND DEALER AT BENITO Y MONJARDIN MADRID

This should alleviate pressure on the peseta but at least in the longer run I do not think that will be enough. In the yield curve we expect further steepening and that means we expect further rate cuts during the year.
In the future contract if it (10-year bono future) breaks 114.30 it can go to 115.
